title: Kestrel onboarding - contract sprint and SLA triage
topics: Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and data residency
Pricing approval path and procurement sprint
Onboarding timeline and required security artifacts
summary: Introductory contracting and procurement intake for Kestrel Systems. Redwood AE/SE reviewed MSA/DPA touch points, SLA targets (p99 latency, incident response), and procurement approval timeline. Customer raised data residency, SOC2, KMS, SSO integration, and an exception around DPA subprocessing. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send redlined MSA within 3 business days, security pack and SOC2 + penetration test reports, and a draft SLA appendix. Procurement to confirm internal approvers and target vendor sprint week. Follow-up meeting scheduled for 2026-05-21.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim, Priya Desai, Liam Ortega (Redwood) — Marta Ruiz, Jordan Lee, Samir Patel, Evelyn Cho (Kestrel)

Summary (auto): procurement intake, MSA/DPA redlines, SLA appendix, security docs to be shared.

00:00 Alex (Redwood): Okay, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining, I see Kestrel folks are here. Um, quick intro, I'm Alex, AE for Redwood Inference, with Priya our solutions engineer and Liam from our onboarding team.
00:12 Marta (Kestrel): Hi all, thanks. We're hoping to move fast — procurement asked for a vendor sprint next week — so want to align on contract items and security.
00:20 Alex: Great, that's the goal. Quick run of agenda: MSA redlines, DPA items, SLA targets, pricing approvals and timeline. Priya, do you want to call out anything infra/security wise?
00:29 Priya (Redwood): Yep, hi everyone — I'll outline SOC2, pentest, KMS and VPC options. We support hosted, dedicated and private deployments; for sensitive data customers often want VPC or on-prem notes.
00:40 Jordan (Kestrel): Quick thing — we need to confirm data residency and subprocessor list. Our legal may want DPA exceptions around logging retention for audit reasons.
00:48 Samir (Kestrel): Also, can you confirm whether Redwood supports customer-managed KMS keys in your private deployment? Our security policy requires bring-your-own-key for production.
00:57 Priya: Yes, BYOK is supported for Private deployments; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with our KMS but can integrate with customer KMS via HSM in Dedicated/Private depending on the deployment. I'll add the exact integration steps to the security pack.
01:12 Alex: On the contracting side — typical MSA redlines for enterprises are around liability caps, IP carve-outs, and data handling. We try to keep standard language but can take a look at Samir's preferred language. Samir, did you have specific redlines prepared?
01:25 Samir: We have a list, yes — main ask is to limit data subprocessor notifications, and tighten breach notification timelines to 48 hours. Also, we may need a carveout for certain telemetry that's PII-adjacent.
01:38 Alex: Understood. Our standard breach notification is 72 hours; 48 is doable but we need to confirm with engineering for our fallback processes. Priya, is 48 workable operationally?
01:47 Priya: Hm, 48 is tight but probably achievable if we set the right on-call and escalation. For Hosted we'd rely on our operational runbook; for Dedicated/Private, the customer usually has more control over logs. I'll flag where automation can help bring it under 48.
02:05 Marta: Procurement also asked for an SLA appendix with clear p99 and p50 latency numbers, uptime, and incident response windows. What's Redwood's standard?
02:14 Priya: For Dedicated we publish p99 numbers in our console — typical target is 200–400ms depending on model and sequence length. For Hosted, there's variable based on model. We can include an SLA appendix that specifies service tiers, support response (P1 1 hour ack, 4 hour remediation window for high-sev) and credits.
02:33 Evelyn (Kestrel): On the credits — procurement needs the math on credits and escalation to finance for pricing approvals. Can you surface that in the appendix?
02:40 Alex: Absolutely. We'll put a pricing table and credit calculation examples. Also note, pricing for Dedicated has commit tiers; if you sign a reserved capacity we can lock price.
02:52 Jordan: Another technical ask — does Redwood provide audit logs that are exportable to our SIEM? We need retention to be configurable to 12 months.
03:01 Priya: Yes, audit logs are exportable, we support syslog/S3 pushes and can tune retention. For Hosted there's a retention default, but for Dedicated/Private we can make it configurable.
03:12 Samir: About subprocessors — we need the list and whether any subprocessors access unredacted customer data. That's a big procurement check.
03:20 Alex: We'll include the current list and indicate access level for each. Note that some model hosting partners may have limited access, but we can flag which vendors are involved in handling raw logs versus aggregated telemetry.
03:34 Marta: Procurement timeline — our vendor sprint week is the 25th. We need to get legal sign-off before that or at least final MSA redlines. Can Redwood commit to a contract sprint in the week of 18th or 25th?
03:46 Alex: We can target sending redlines by the 19th, then aim for a follow-up review on the 21st and sprint the 25th. That fits our legal cadence.
03:55 Liam (Redwood): I'll prepare an onboarding checklist and a pilot support plan so your procurement can see the steps we take during initial integration.
04:03 Evelyn: For private deployments — can you confirm networking requirements? We need a list of subnet/CIDR ranges and egress rules for our firewall team.
04:12 Priya: Sure, I'll attach an infra note with specific ports, CIDRs, and required access. For VPC peering we have documented steps.
04:20 Samir: DPA question — do you have an annex for EU data residency? Some of our customers are EU-based and we need a clear subprocessor and residency guarantee.
04:29 Alex: We have region controls and can pin deployments to regions; however, model variants and fallbacks are important — we'll call out region pinning in the DPA appendix.
04:39 Jordan: Pen testing — do you share pentest exec summaries? We can't accept redacted or partial reports; procurement needs enough to assess risk.
04:46 Priya: We can share an executive pentest summary and SOC2 Type II report under an NDA; full detailed findings are shared with customers under a controlled disclosure when necessary.
04:58 Marta: Who's the internal approver matrix at Redwood for DPA exceptions? Procurement needs to know who signs off on changes to data retention and subprocessors.
05:08 Alex: Typically the AE can intake minor DPA notes, legal and security review larger exceptions. I'll note Samir's exceptions and route them. We'll include a point of contact in the cover email.
05:18 Samir: For liability caps, we typically target a 2x ARR cap for SaaS contracts; is Redwood flexible?
05:25 Alex: We can discuss caps — usually we mirror enterprise norms, and for Dedicated/private we can be more flexible. We'll include proposed language in the redline.
05:33 Marta: Pricing approvals: finance needs a clean list of committed vs variable costs, and a walk-through of potential overage rules.
05:41 Alex: We'll include that in the pricing appendix with sample invoices. Also will call out how caching, batching, and quantization recommendations affect unit costs — Priya can include a short note.
05:50 Priya: Yep, I'll add quantization options and expected cost delta for typical workloads.
06:00 Jordan: Quick ops question — what's your incident communication channel? Do we get a dedicated slack?
06:06 Liam: For Dedicated customers we can set up a dedicated Slack/Teams channel and PagerDuty integration. We'll include escalation matrix in the onboarding plan.
06:16 Marta: Ok, sounds good. A couple of procurement procedural items: We need Redwood to fill out our vendor intake form and sign a standard MSA with DPA. Can you do the vendor intake before sending redlines?
06:27 Alex: Yes, we'll fill your intake form. Can you share the link?
06:30 Marta: I'll send it after this call.
06:33 Alex: Great. To recap quickly: Redwood to send redlined MSA + SLA appendix, security pack (SOC2, pentest summary, KMS notes), onboarding checklist, and pricing appendix. Kestrel to share DPA exception list and vendor intake form. Follow-up next Thursday 2026-05-21 for review.
06:50 Samir: One last point — if there are any special data flow diagrams, we need them for our privacy office.
06:55 Priya: We'll attach an architecture diagram showing data at rest/encryption boundaries for the deployment model you choose.
07:02 Alex: Awesome. Thanks everyone, we'll get those artifacts over.
07:06 Marta: Thanks, bye.
07:08 End of call.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels, stutters and overlapping talk; some technical terms transcribed roughly (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes as "key V cache"). Links referenced: (redwood-sec-pack) https://redwood.share/secure/pack (placeholder), vendor intake: https://kestrel.share/vendor-intake (placeholder).
